source.text: אַל־תְּ֭קַנֵּא בְּאַנְשֵׁ֣י רָעָ֑ה וְאַל־תִּ֝תְאָ֗יו לִהְי֥וֹת אִתָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not be jealous of people of evil, and do not desire to be with them,

en.L: Do not envy people of evil, \q and do not desire to be with them,
en.B: Do not be envious of evil people \q or wish you could be with them,
en.R: Do not be jealous of evil people. \q Do not want to be their friend.

fr.L: N’envie pas les gens du mal, \q et ne désire pas être avec eux,
fr.B: Ne sois pas jaloux des méchants \q et ne souhaite pas être en leur compagnie,
fr.R: Ne sois pas jaloux des gens mauvais. \q Ne cherche pas à devenir leur ami.

sw.L: Usiwaonee wivu watu wa uovu, \q wala usitamani kuwa pamoja nao,
sw.B: Usiwaonee wivu watu waovu \q wala usitamani kuwa pamoja nao,
sw.R: Usiwaonee wivu watu waovu. \q Usitamani kuwa rafiki yao.

decisions.choice: desire, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The sense is the same (23:6).

decisions.choice: do not envy evil people: as in 23:17
decisions.reason: Compare 3:31; 24:19; Psalm 37:1.

source.text: כִּי־שֹׁ֭דיֶהְגֶּ֣ה לִבָּ֑ם וְ֝עָמָ֗ל שִׂפְתֵיהֶ֥ם תְּדַבֵּֽרְנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: for violence their heart plots, and trouble their lips speak.

en.L: for their heart plots violence, \q and their lips speak trouble.
en.B: because their minds are set on violence \q and their talk is all about causing harm.
en.R: They are always thinking of ways to hurt people. \q They talk about making trouble.

fr.L: car leur cœur médite la violence, \q et leurs lèvres parlent de nuire.
fr.B: car ils ne pensent qu’à la violence \q et ne parlent que de faire du mal.
fr.R: Ils cherchent toujours comment faire du mal aux autres. \q Ils parlent de causer des ennuis.

sw.L: kwa maana moyo wao unapanga jeuri, \q na midomo yao inasema taabu.
sw.B: kwa sababu akili zao zimeelekea kwenye jeuri, \q na maneno yao yote ni ya kuleta madhara.
sw.R: Daima wanawaza njia za kuwaumiza watu. \q Wanazungumza juu ya kuleta matatizo.

decisions.choice: violence ... trouble: harm done to others
decisions.reason: The pair (shod, amal) means destruction and the misery it brings (Psalm 10:7; Isaiah 59:7).

source.text: בְּ֭חָכְמָה יִבָּ֣נֶה בָּ֑יִת וּ֝בִתְבוּנָ֗ה יִתְכּוֹנָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: By wisdom is built a house, and by understanding it is established;

en.L: By wisdom a house is built, \q and by understanding it is established;
en.B: A house is built through wisdom \q and made secure through understanding;
en.R: Wisdom is what builds a home. \q Understanding is what makes it strong.

fr.L: Par la sagesse une maison est bâtie, \q et par l’intelligence elle est affermie ;
fr.B: C’est avec la sagesse qu’on bâtit une maison, \q et avec l’intelligence qu’on l’affermit ;
fr.R: C’est la sagesse qui bâtit une famille. \q C’est l’intelligence qui la rend solide.

sw.L: Kwa hekima nyumba hujengwa, \q na kwa ufahamu huimarishwa;
sw.B: Nyumba hujengwa kwa hekima \q na kuthibitishwa kwa ufahamu;
sw.R: Hekima ndiyo inayojenga nyumba. \q Ufahamu ndio unaoifanya iwe imara.

decisions.choice: a house: a building, and the household in it
decisions.reason: As in 14:1, the house is both the building and the family. Wisdom built her own house in 9:1, and the LORD founded the earth by wisdom in 3:19–20.

decisions.choice: "une famille" at Readable
decisions.reason: French "maison" can mean the household, but young readers hear the building; the English Readable "home" carries both. Meaning decision m1 says the house is the building and the family in it; Readable names the family, since verse 4 fills it with good things.

source.text: וּ֭בְדַעַת חֲדָרִ֣ים יִמָּלְא֑וּ כָּל־ה֖וֹן יָקָ֣ר וְנָעִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: and by knowledge rooms are filled [with] all wealth precious and pleasant.

en.L: and by knowledge [the] rooms are filled \q [with] all [kinds of] precious and pleasant wealth.
en.B: by knowledge its rooms are filled \q with every kind of rich and lovely treasure.
en.R: Knowledge fills it with all kinds of beautiful and valuable things.

fr.L: et par la connaissance [les] chambres sont remplies \q de toute [sorte de] richesse précieuse et agréable.
fr.B: par la connaissance ses chambres se remplissent \q de toutes sortes de trésors riches et beaux.
fr.R: La connaissance la remplit de toutes sortes de choses belles et précieuses.

sw.L: na kwa maarifa vyumba hujazwa \q [kila aina ya] mali yenye thamani na ya kupendeza.
sw.B: kwa maarifa vyumba vyake hujazwa \q kila aina ya hazina ya thamani na nzuri.
sw.R: Maarifa huijaza kila aina ya vitu vizuri vya thamani.

decisions.choice: precious and pleasant wealth: the reward wisdom brings
decisions.reason: Compare 8:18, 21 and 1:13, where robbers hope to fill their houses by violence.

source.text: גֶּֽבֶר־חָכָ֥ם בַּע֑וֹז וְאִֽישׁ־דַּ֝֗עַת מְאַמֶּץ־כֹּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: A man wise [is] in strength, and a person of knowledge [is] making firm strength.

en.L: A wise man [is] strong, \q and a person of knowledge increases {{gender:their|his}} strength.
en.B: Wise people have great power, \q and those with knowledge grow ever stronger.
en.R: Wisdom makes people strong. \q Knowledge makes them even stronger.

fr.L: Un homme sage [est] dans la force, \q et un homme de connaissance affermit sa force.
fr.B: Les gens sages ont une grande force, \q et ceux qui ont la connaissance deviennent toujours plus forts.
fr.R: La sagesse rend les gens forts. \q La connaissance les rend encore plus forts.

sw.L: Mwanamume mwenye hekima [ni] hodari, \q na mtu wa maarifa huongeza nguvu zake.
sw.B: Watu wenye hekima wana nguvu nyingi, \q na wenye maarifa huzidi kuwa na nguvu.
sw.R: Hekima huwafanya watu wawe na nguvu. \q Maarifa huwafanya wawe na nguvu zaidi.

decisions.choice: is strong: has strength
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "a wise man is in strength". The ancient Greek translation reads "a wise man is better than a strong one", which fits 16:32 and 21:22.

decisions.choice: "un homme sage", "un homme de connaissance" at Literal, without a gender setting
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has two words for "man" here (*gever*, *ish*), and the English Literal keeps "man". French Literal keeps "homme" for both; Balanced and Readable say "les gens", which includes everyone, as the English does.

source.text: כִּ֣י בְ֭תַחְבֻּלוֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה־לְּךָ֣ מִלְחָמָ֑ה וּ֝תְשׁוּעָ֗ה בְּרֹ֣ב יוֹעֵֽץ׃

records.literal_gloss: For by guidance you will make for yourself war, and victory [is] in a multitude of counselors.

en.L: For by guidance you will wage your war, \q and victory [is] in many counselors.
en.B: You should wage war with careful guidance; \q victory comes from having many advisers.
en.R: Before you go to war, get good advice. \q You win when many people give you advice.

fr.L: Car par de sages directives tu feras ta guerre, \q et la victoire [est] dans le grand nombre de conseillers.
fr.B: C’est avec des directives sages qu’il faut faire la guerre ; \q la victoire vient d’avoir beaucoup de conseillers.
fr.R: Avant de partir en guerre, demande de bons conseils. \q On gagne quand beaucoup de gens nous conseillent.

sw.L: Kwa maana kwa maongozi utapigana vita vyako, \q na ushindi [uko] katika washauri wengi.
sw.B: Pigana vita kwa maongozi ya busara; \q ushindi hutokana na kuwa na washauri wengi.
sw.R: Kabla ya kwenda vitani, pata shauri jema. \q Unashinda watu wengi wanapokushauri.

decisions.choice: guidance ... many counselors: as in 11:14 and 20:18
decisions.reason: The word for guidance (tahbulot) is a sailor's word, steering (1:5). Strength in verse 5 comes from good counsel, not from force.

source.text: רָאמ֣וֹת לֶֽאֱוִ֣יל חָכְמ֑וֹת בַּ֝שַּׁ֗עַר לֹ֣א יִפְתַּח־פִּֽיהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: High for a fool [are] wisdom; in the gate he does not open his mouth.

en.L: Wisdom [is too] high for a fool; \q in the gate {{gender:they do|he does}} not open {{gender:their|his}} mouth.
en.B: Wisdom is out of a fool's reach; \q at the city gate, where matters are decided, \q the fool has nothing to say.
en.R: Wisdom is too hard for fools to reach. \q When leaders meet to make decisions, fools have nothing to say.

fr.L: La sagesse [est trop] haute pour l’insensé ; \q à la porte il n’ouvre pas la bouche.
fr.B: La sagesse est hors de portée de l’insensé ; \q à la porte de la ville, où l’on décide des affaires, \q l’insensé n’a rien à dire.
fr.R: La sagesse est trop difficile à atteindre pour les insensés. \q Quand les chefs se réunissent pour décider, les insensés n’ont rien à dire.

sw.L: Hekima [iko juu mno] kwa mpumbavu; \q langoni hafumbui kinywa chake.
sw.B: Hekima iko mbali, mpumbavu hawezi kuifikia; \q langoni pa mji, mambo yanapoamuliwa, \q mpumbavu hana la kusema.
sw.R: Hekima ni ngumu mno kwa wapumbavu kuifikia. \q Viongozi wanapokutana kufanya maamuzi, wapumbavu hawana la kusema.

decisions.choice: high: out of reach
decisions.reason: Wisdom is like something on a high shelf: the fool (evil) cannot reach it. The plural form of "wisdom" is used of Wisdom herself in 1:20 and 9:1.

decisions.choice: the gate: where the town met to decide matters
decisions.reason: The elders sat in the city gate to judge cases and discuss public affairs (31:23; Ruth 4:1–2).

source.text: מְחַשֵּׁ֥ב לְהָרֵ֑עַ ל֝֗וֹ בַּֽעַל־מְזִמּ֥וֹת יִקְרָֽאוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [One who] plans to do evil, him master of plots they will call.

en.L: Whoever plans to do evil, \q people will call {{gender:them|him}} a master of schemes.
en.B: Whoever plots to do evil \q will be known as a schemer.
en.R: People who plan evil things will get a name for being troublemakers.

fr.L: Celui qui projette de faire le mal, \q on l’appellera un maître en intrigues.
fr.B: Celui qui complote pour faire le mal \q sera connu comme un intrigant.
fr.R: Ceux qui préparent de mauvais coups auront la réputation de fauteurs de troubles.

sw.L: Yeye apangaye kutenda mabaya, \q watu watamwita bingwa wa hila.
sw.B: Yeyote anayepanga kutenda maovu \q atajulikana kuwa mtu wa hila.
sw.R: Watu wanaopanga mambo mabaya watapata sifa ya kuwa wachochezi wa matatizo.

decisions.choice: master of schemes: a known schemer
decisions.reason: The word (mezimmah) can mean good discretion (1:4) but here means evil plotting (12:2; 14:17).

source.text: זִמַּ֣ת אִוֶּ֣לֶת חַטָּ֑את וְתוֹעֲבַ֖ת לְאָדָ֣ם לֵֽץ׃

records.literal_gloss: A plan of foolishness [is] sin, and an abomination to humankind [is] a mocker.

en.L: [The] scheming of folly [is] sin, \q and [the] mocker [is] an abomination to people.
en.B: Foolish scheming is sin, \q and people detest a mocker.
en.R: Planning foolish things is a sin. \q Everyone hates a person who makes fun of others.

fr.L: Le projet de la folie [est] péché, \q et le moqueur [est] une abomination pour les humains.
fr.B: Les projets insensés sont un péché, \q et les gens détestent le moqueur.
fr.R: Préparer des choses insensées, c’est un péché. \q Tout le monde déteste celui qui se moque des autres.

sw.L: Hila ya upumbavu [ni] dhambi, \q na mwenye dharau [ni] chukizo kwa wanadamu.
sw.B: Kupanga upumbavu ni dhambi, \q na watu humchukia mwenye dharau.
sw.R: Kupanga mambo ya kipumbavu ni dhambi. \q Kila mtu humchukia mtu anayewadharau wengine.

decisions.choice: the scheming of folly: foolish plans, or the plans of a fool
decisions.reason: Either way, the plan itself is already sin, before it is carried out.

decisions.choice: "le moqueur" for *lets* at every level, for the whole book; Readable explains it, "celui qui se moque des autres"
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets. "Railleur" is more literary; "moqueur" is the common word.

decisions.choice: "mwenye dharau" (one full of contempt) for the mocker (lets) at Literal and Balanced; Readable describes him
decisions.reason: "Mwenye mzaha" can sound like someone who merely jokes; the mocker of Proverbs scorns correction and looks down on others, which "dharau" says. This is the word for the mocker throughout Proverbs.

source.text: הִ֭תְרַפִּיתָ בְּי֥וֹם צָרָ֗ה צַ֣ר כֹּחֶֽכָה׃

records.literal_gloss: You have shown yourself without courage in a day of trouble; narrow [is] your strength.

en.L: [If] you lose heart in [the] day of trouble, \q your strength [is] small.
en.B: If you give up when times are hard, \q how little strength you have!
en.R: If you give up when life gets hard, you are not very strong.

fr.L: [Si] tu faiblis au jour de la détresse, \q ta force [est] mince.
fr.B: Si tu perds courage aux jours difficiles, \q que ta force est petite !
fr.R: Si tu abandonnes quand la vie devient dure, tu n’es pas très fort.

sw.L: [Ukilegea] siku ya taabu, \q nguvu zako [ni] chache.
sw.B: Ukikata tamaa nyakati za shida, \q nguvu zako ni ndogo kweli!
sw.R: Ukikata tamaa maisha yanapokuwa magumu, huna nguvu nyingi.

decisions.choice: day of trouble ... your strength is small: a play on words
decisions.reason: "Trouble" (tsarah) and "small", literally "narrow" (tsar), sound alike: a narrow time shows a narrow strength. The verse leads into verses 11–12.

decisions.choice: "au jour de la détresse ... ta force [est] mince"
alternatives: "au jour de l'angoisse ... ta force est étroite"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plays on two words from one root, *tsarah* "trouble" and *tsar* "narrow" (meaning decision m1). French cannot keep the pun; "détresse" and "mince" at least keep the picture of being squeezed.

source.text: הַ֭צֵּל לְקֻחִ֣ים לַמָּ֑וֶת וּמָטִ֥ים לַ֝הֶ֗רֶג אִם־תַּחְשֽׂוֹךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Deliver [those who are being] taken to death, and [those who are] staggering to slaughter, if you will restrain.

en.L: Rescue [those who are being] taken to death, \q and [those] staggering to [the] slaughter, \q oh hold [them] back!
en.B: Rescue those being dragged off to death; \q hold back those who are stumbling toward slaughter.
en.R: Save people who are being led away to be killed. \q Do whatever you can to stop it.

fr.L: Délivre [ceux qu’on] emmène à la mort, \q et [ceux qui] chancellent vers le massacre, \q oh, retiens-[les] !
fr.B: Délivre ceux qu’on traîne vers la mort ; \q retiens ceux qui titubent vers le massacre.
fr.R: Sauve les gens qu’on emmène pour les tuer. \q Fais tout ce que tu peux pour l’empêcher.

sw.L: Okoa [wale wanaochukuliwa] kwenye kifo, \q na [wale] wanaoyumbayumba kuelekea machinjoni, \q laiti ungewazuia!
sw.B: Waokoe wanaoburutwa kwenda kuuawa; \q wazuie wale wanaojikokota kuelekea machinjoni.
sw.R: Waokoe watu wanaopelekwa kuuawa. \q Fanya lolote uwezalo kuzuia jambo hilo.

decisions.choice: oh hold them back: an urgent plea
decisions.reason: The words "if you hold back" can be a wish, "if only you would hold them back", or the start of the excuse answered in verse 12: "if you hold back, saying ...".

decisions.choice: taken to death: the innocent in danger of death
decisions.reason: The verse does not say who they are; the point is the duty to act for those whose lives are at risk (31:8–9).

source.text: כִּֽי־תֹאמַ֗ר הֵן֮ לֹא־יָדַ֪עְנ֫וּ זֶ֥ה הֲֽלֹא־תֹ֘כֵ֤ן לִבּ֨וֹת׀הֽוּא־יָבִ֗ין וְנֹצֵ֣ר נַ֭פְשְׁךָ ה֣וּא יֵדָ֑ע וְהֵשִׁ֖יב לְאָדָ֣ם כְּפָעֳלֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: If you will say, Here! not we knew this, [does] not [the one who] weighs hearts he perceive? And [the one who] guards your life he does he know? And will he repay to a person according to his work?

en.L: If you say, "Look, we did not know this," \q does not [the one who] weighs hearts perceive [it]? \q [Does] not [the one who] guards your life know [it]? \q And will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not repay [each] person according to {{gender:their|his}} work?
en.B: If you say, "But we knew nothing about this," \q does not the one who weighs hearts see the truth? \q The one who watches over your life knows it well, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will repay each person for what they have done.
en.R: You may say, "We did not know." \q But God sees what is in your heart. \q He watches over your life, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows. \q He will pay back everyone for what they have done.

fr.L: Si tu dis : « Voici, nous ne savions pas cela », \q celui qui pèse les cœurs ne [le] discerne-t-il pas ? \q Celui qui garde ton âme ne [le] sait-il pas ? \q Et ne rendra-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pas à [chaque] homme selon son œuvre ?
fr.B: Si tu dis : « Mais nous n’en savions rien », \q celui qui pèse les cœurs ne voit-il pas la vérité ? \q Celui qui veille sur ta vie le sait bien, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rendra à chacun selon ce qu’il a fait.
fr.R: Tu diras peut-être : « Nous ne savions pas. » \q Mais Dieu voit ce qu’il y a dans ton cœur. \q Il veille sur ta vie, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sait. \q Il rendra à chacun ce que mérite ce qu’il a fait.

sw.L: Ukisema, "Tazama, hatukujua jambo hili," \q je, [yeye] apimaye mioyo hatambui? \q Je, [yeye] aulindaye uhai wako hajui? \q Na je, hatamlipa [kila] mtu kwa kadiri ya kazi yake?
sw.B: Ukisema, "Lakini sisi hatukujua lolote juu ya jambo hili," \q je, yeye apimaye mioyo haoni ukweli? \q Yeye aulindaye uhai wako anajua vizuri, \q {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atamlipa kila mtu kwa kadiri ya alichotenda.
sw.R: Unaweza kusema, "Hatukujua." \q Lakini Mungu anaona kilicho moyoni mwako. \q Yeye huulinda uhai wako, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} anajua. \q Atamlipa kila mtu kwa kadiri ya alichotenda.

decisions.choice: the one who weighs hearts: God, who sees motives
decisions.reason: As in 16:2 and 21:2, God tests the heart and cannot be put off with excuses. He who keeps the listener alive will hold the listener to account (Psalm 62:13; Romans 2:6).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God, whom the description plainly means.

decisions.choice: "à [chaque] homme selon son œuvre" at Literal, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The Hebrew *adam* means any human being. At Literal French keeps the generic "homme" after "chaque", where it plainly means each person, and "son" refers back to it without a setting; Balanced and Readable say "chacun".

source.text: אֱכָל־בְּנִ֣י דְבַ֣שׁ כִּי־ט֑וֹב וְנֹ֥פֶת מָ֝ת֗וֹק עַל־חִכֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Eat, my son, honey, for [it is] good, and honey from the comb [is] sweet on your palate.

en.L: Eat honey, my son, for [it is] good, \q and honey from the comb [is] sweet to your taste.
en.B: My son, eat honey, because it is good; \q honey from the comb tastes sweet.
en.R: My son, eat honey, because it is good. \q It tastes sweet.

fr.L: Mange du miel, mon fils, car [il est] bon, \q et le miel du rayon [est] doux à ton palais.
fr.B: Mon fils, mange du miel, car il est bon ; \q le miel qui coule du rayon a un goût doux.
fr.R: Mon fils, mange du miel, parce que c’est bon. \q Il a un goût sucré.

sw.L: Kula asali, mwanangu, kwa maana [ni] nzuri, \q na asali ya sega [ni] tamu kwa ulimi wako.
sw.B: Mwanangu, kula asali, kwa sababu ni nzuri; \q asali ya sega ina ladha tamu.
sw.R: Mwanangu, kula asali, kwa sababu ni nzuri. \q Ina ladha tamu.

decisions.choice: honey from the comb: the purest honey
decisions.reason: The word (nophet) is honey dripping from the comb (5:3; Psalm 19:11). The pleasure of honey leads into the comparison of verse 14.

source.text: כֵּ֤ן׀דְּעֶ֥ה חָכְמָ֗ה לְנַ֫פְשֶׁ֥ךָ אִם־מָ֭צָאתָ וְיֵ֣שׁ אַחֲרִ֑ית וְ֝תִקְוָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תִכָּרֵֽת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Thus know wisdom for your soul; if you find [it], there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.

en.L: So know [that] wisdom [is such] for your soul; \q if you find [it], there is a future, \q and your hope will not be cut off.
en.B: Know that wisdom is like that for your soul: \q find it, and you will have a future, \q and your hope will not fail.
en.R: Wisdom is just as sweet for your life. \q If you find it, you will have a good future. \q What you hope for will come true.

fr.L: Ainsi, sache [que] la sagesse [est telle] pour ton âme ; \q si tu [la] trouves, il y a un avenir, \q et ton espérance ne sera pas retranchée.
fr.B: Sache qu’il en est ainsi de la sagesse pour ton âme : \q trouve-la, et tu auras un avenir, \q et ton espérance ne sera pas déçue.
fr.R: La sagesse est aussi douce pour ta vie. \q Si tu la trouves, tu auras un bel avenir. \q Ce que tu espères se réalisera.

sw.L: Basi ujue [kwamba] hekima [ni hivyo] kwa nafsi yako; \q ukiipata, kuna wakati ujao, \q na tumaini lako halitakatiliwa mbali.
sw.B: Ujue kwamba hekima ni hivyo kwa nafsi yako: \q ukiipata, utakuwa na wakati ujao, \q na tumaini lako halitapotea.
sw.R: Hekima ni tamu vivyo hivyo kwa maisha yako. \q Ukiipata, utakuwa na kesho njema. \q Unachokitumainia kitatimia.

decisions.choice: a future ... your hope will not be cut off: as in 23:18
decisions.reason: The second half repeats 23:18 almost word for word.

source.text: אַל־תֶּאֱרֹ֣ב רָ֭שָׁע לִנְוֵ֣ה צַדִּ֑יק אַֽל־תְּשַׁדֵּ֥ד רִבְצוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not lie in wait, wicked [person], at [the] habitation of a righteous [person]; do not devastate his resting place.

en.L: Do not lie in wait, wicked [one], at [the] home of [the] righteous; \q do not destroy {{gender:their|his}} resting place.
en.B: Do not lie in ambush like a criminal at the home of a righteous person; \q do not raid the place where they live.
en.R: Do not wait in hiding to attack the home of a good person, as wicked people do. \q Do not wreck the place where they live.

fr.L: Ne guette pas, méchant, la demeure du juste ; \q ne dévaste pas son lieu de repos.
fr.B: Ne tends pas d’embuscade comme un malfaiteur près de la maison du juste ; \q ne saccage pas l’endroit où il vit.
fr.R: Ne te cache pas pour attaquer la maison d’une personne honnête, comme le font les méchants. \q Ne détruis pas l’endroit où elle vit.

sw.L: Usivizie, [ewe] mwovu, kwenye makao ya mwenye haki; \q usiharibu mahali pake pa kupumzika.
sw.B: Usivizie kama mhalifu kwenye nyumba ya mtu mwenye haki; \q usivamie mahali anapoishi.
sw.R: Usijifiche ukingoja kushambulia nyumba ya mtu mwema, kama waovu wafanyavyo. \q Usiharibu mahali anapoishi.

decisions.choice: wicked one: addressed to the wicked, or warning against acting like one
decisions.reason: The word may be a call to a wicked person, or describe the one the listener must not become.

source.text: כִּ֤י שֶׁ֨בַע׀יִפּ֣וֹל צַדִּ֣יק וָקָ֑ם וּ֝רְשָׁעִ֗ים יִכָּשְׁל֥וּ בְרָעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For seven [times] a righteous [person] will fall and rise, but wicked [people] will stumble in trouble.

en.L: For seven [times] a righteous [person] falls and rises [again], \q but [the] wicked stumble in disaster.
en.B: For the righteous may fall seven times and still get up again, \q but the wicked are brought down by calamity.
en.R: Good people may fall again and again, but they will get back up. \q Wicked people are ruined when trouble comes.

fr.L: Car le juste tombe sept [fois] et se relève, \q mais les méchants trébuchent dans le malheur.
fr.B: Car le juste peut tomber sept fois et se relever encore, \q mais les méchants sont renversés par le malheur.
fr.R: Les gens honnêtes peuvent tomber encore et encore, mais ils se relèvent. \q Les méchants sont détruits quand le malheur arrive.

sw.L: Kwa maana mwenye haki huanguka mara saba na kuinuka [tena], \q lakini waovu hujikwaa katika msiba.
sw.B: Kwa maana mwenye haki anaweza kuanguka mara saba na bado akainuka tena, \q lakini waovu huangushwa na msiba.
sw.R: Watu wema wanaweza kuanguka tena na tena, lakini wataamka tena. \q Watu waovu huangamia taabu inapokuja.

decisions.choice: falls seven times: meets trouble again and again
decisions.reason: To fall here is to meet misfortune, not to sin. Seven is the number of fullness: however often the righteous are knocked down, they rise. The wicked fall once and stay down.

decisions.choice: "le juste" (Literal, Balanced), "les gens honnêtes" (Readable); "les méchants" at every level, for the whole book
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for *tsaddiq* and *reshaim*. The Readable level follows the English "good people" with an ordinary French word for someone who does right.

source.text: בִּנְפֹ֣ל אֽ֭וֹיִבְךָאַל־תִּשְׂמָ֑ח וּ֝בִכָּשְׁל֗וֹ אַל־יָגֵ֥ל לִבֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: When your enemy falls, do not rejoice, and when he stumbles, let not your heart be glad,

en.L: When your enemy falls, do not rejoice, \q and when {{gender:they stumble|he stumbles}}, do not let your heart be glad,
en.B: When your enemy falls, do not celebrate; \q when they trip up, do not let your heart be glad,
en.R: Do not be happy when your enemy falls. \q Do not be glad when they get into trouble.

fr.L: Quand ton ennemi tombe, ne te réjouis pas, \q et quand il trébuche, que ton cœur ne soit pas dans l’allégresse,
fr.B: Quand ton ennemi tombe, ne fais pas la fête ; \q quand il trébuche, que ton cœur ne s’en réjouisse pas,
fr.R: Ne sois pas content quand ton ennemi tombe. \q Ne te réjouis pas quand il a des ennuis.

sw.L: Adui yako akianguka, usifurahi, \q na akijikwaa, moyo wako usishangilie,
sw.B: Adui yako akianguka, usisherehekee; \q akijikwaa, moyo wako usifurahi,
sw.R: Usifurahi adui yako anapoanguka. \q Usishangilie anapopatwa na taabu.

decisions.choice: your enemy, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written form has the plural; the sense is the same.

source.text: פֶּן־יִרְאֶ֣ה יְ֭הוָה וְרַ֣ע בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְהֵשִׁ֖יב מֵעָלָ֣יו אַפּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: lest YHWH should see, and it will be displeasing in his eyes, and he will turn back from on him his anger.

en.L: or {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will see, and [it will be] evil in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will turn {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger away from {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: or {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will see it and be displeased, \q and turn {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger away from them.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will see it and will not like it. \q Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may stop being angry with your enemy.

fr.L: de peur que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne voie, et [que ce ne soit] mal à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} yeux, \q et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne détourne de lui {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère.
fr.B: car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} le verrait et en serait mécontent, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} détournerait de lui {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} le verra et n’aimera pas cela. \q Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pourrait cesser d’être en colère contre ton ennemi.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asije akaona, ikawa [ni] ovu machoni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}}, \q akaiondoa hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwake.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asije akaona na kuchukizwa, \q akaiondoa hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwake.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ataona jambo hilo na hatalipenda. \q Kisha anaweza kuacha kumkasirikia adui yako.

decisions.choice: turn his anger away: gloating is itself a wrong
decisions.reason: The saying does not teach how to make an enemy suffer more. It shows that the LORD hates gloating, and the one who gloats may find God's displeasure turned on themselves (17:5; Job 31:29).

source.text: אַל־תִּתְחַ֥ר בַּמְּרֵעִ֑ים אַל־תְּ֝קַנֵּ֗א בָּרְשָׁעִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not fret yourself because of evildoers; do not be jealous of the wicked,

en.L: Do not fret because of evildoers; \q do not envy the wicked,
en.B: Do not get upset about those who do evil \q or be envious of the wicked,
en.R: Do not worry about people who do evil. \q Do not be jealous of them.

fr.L: Ne t’irrite pas à cause des malfaiteurs ; \q n’envie pas les méchants,
fr.B: Ne te mets pas en colère à cause de ceux qui font le mal, \q et ne sois pas jaloux des méchants,
fr.R: Ne t’inquiète pas à cause des gens qui font le mal. \q Ne sois pas jaloux d’eux.

sw.L: Usijisumbue kwa sababu ya watenda maovu; \q usiwaonee wivu waovu,
sw.B: Usikasirike kwa sababu ya wale wanaotenda maovu \q wala usiwaonee wivu waovu,
sw.R: Usihangaike kwa sababu ya watu wanaotenda maovu. \q Usiwaonee wivu.

decisions.choice: do not fret ... do not envy: as in Psalm 37:1
decisions.reason: The verse echoes Psalm 37:1 and repeats the theme of verse 1 and 23:17.

source.text: כִּ֤י׀לֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֣ה אַחֲרִ֣ית לָרָ֑ע נֵ֖ר רְשָׁעִ֣ים יִדְעָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: for there will not be a future for the evil [person]; [the] lamp of wicked [people] will be extinguished.

en.L: for there will be no future for the evil [person]; \q [the] lamp of [the] wicked will be put out.
en.B: for evil people have no future; \q the lamp of the wicked will go out.
en.R: Evil people have no future. \q Their lives will end like a lamp that goes out.

fr.L: car il n’y aura pas d’avenir pour le mauvais ; \q la lampe des méchants s’éteindra.
fr.B: car les gens mauvais n’ont pas d’avenir ; \q la lampe des méchants s’éteindra.
fr.R: Les gens mauvais n’ont pas d’avenir. \q Leur vie finira comme une lampe qui s’éteint.

sw.L: kwa maana mtu mwovu hatakuwa na wakati ujao; \q taa ya waovu itazimwa.
sw.B: kwa maana watu waovu hawana wakati ujao; \q taa ya waovu itazimika.
sw.R: Watu waovu hawana kesho. \q Maisha yao yataisha kama taa inayozimika.

decisions.choice: the lamp ... put out: life and family come to an end
decisions.reason: As in 13:9 and 20:20. The "future" (aharit) is the one promised to the wise in verse 14 and 23:18.

source.text: יְרָֽא־אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה בְּנִ֣י וָמֶ֑לֶךְ עִם־שׁ֝וֹנִ֗ים אַל־תִּתְעָרָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: Fear YHWH, my son, and the king; with [those who] change do not get involved,

en.L: Fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my son, and the king; \q do not get involved with those who are given to change,
en.B: Fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the king, my son, \q and have nothing to do with those who want to overturn things,
en.R: My son, honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with awe, and respect the king. \q Do not join with people who rebel against them.

fr.L: Crains {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, mon fils, et le roi ; \q ne te mêle pas à ceux qui aiment le changement,
fr.B: Crains {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et le roi, mon fils, \q et n’aie rien à faire avec ceux qui veulent tout renverser,
fr.R: Mon fils, honore {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avec respect, et respecte le roi. \q Ne te joins pas aux gens qui se révoltent contre eux.

sw.L: Mche {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mwanangu, na mfalme; \q usijiunge na wale wanaopenda mabadiliko,
sw.B: Mche {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na mfalme, mwanangu, \q wala usishirikiane na wale wanaotaka kupindua mambo,
sw.R: Mwanangu, umheshimu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa hofu takatifu, na umheshimu mfalme. \q Usijiunge na watu wanaowaasi.

decisions.choice: those who are given to change: rebels
alternatives: do not disobey either of them (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The word (shonim) means those who change or are different; here most likely people who stir up revolt against the LORD and the king. The ancient Greek translation reads "do not disobey either of them".

decisions.choice: fear the LORD and the king
decisions.reason: Compare 1 Peter 2:17.

source.text: כִּֽי־פִ֭תְאֹם יָק֣וּם אֵידָ֑ם וּפִ֥יד שְׁ֝נֵיהֶ֗ם מִ֣י יוֹדֵֽעַ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: for suddenly will arise their calamity, and the disaster of both of them, who knows?

en.L: for their calamity will rise up suddenly, \q and who knows the ruin [that comes from] the two of them?
en.B: for disaster will strike them without warning, \q and who can tell what ruin {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the king can bring?
en.R: Those people will suddenly be destroyed. \q No one knows how terrible the punishment from God and the king can be.

fr.L: car leur malheur surgira soudain, \q et qui connaît la ruine [venant] de tous les deux ?
fr.B: car le désastre les frappera sans prévenir, \q et qui peut dire quelle ruine {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et le roi peuvent causer ?
fr.R: Ces gens-là seront soudain détruits. \q Personne ne sait combien la punition de Dieu et du roi peut être terrible.

sw.L: kwa maana msiba wao utainuka ghafula, \q na nani ajuaye maangamizi [yatokayo] kwa hao wawili?
sw.B: kwa maana maafa yatawapata bila onyo, \q na nani awezaye kusema maangamizi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na mfalme wanaweza kuleta?
sw.R: Watu hao wataangamizwa ghafula. \q Hakuna ajuaye jinsi adhabu ya Mungu na ya mfalme inavyoweza kuwa mbaya.

decisions.choice: the ruin of the two of them: ruin sent by the LORD and the king
alternatives: the ruin that comes on both kinds of rebel
decisions.reason: "The two of them" most likely means the LORD and the king of verse 21; it may instead mean the rebels against each. Verse 22 ends the section of "the words of the wise" begun at 22:17.

decisions.choice: the LORD and the king; God and the king
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who is meant.

source.text: גַּם־אֵ֥לֶּה לַֽחֲכָמִ֑ים הַֽכֵּר־פָּנִ֖ים בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט בַּל־טֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: Also these [belong] to wise [people]. To regard faces in judgment [is] not good.

en.L: These also [are sayings] of [the] wise. \q To show partiality in judgment [is] not good.
en.B: These also are sayings of the wise: \q It is not right to show favoritism in a court case.
en.R: Here are more sayings from wise people: \q A judge should not take sides unfairly.

fr.L: Ceux-ci aussi [sont des paroles] des sages. \q Avoir égard aux personnes dans le jugement n’[est] pas bon.
fr.B: Voici encore des paroles des sages : \q Il n’est pas bien de favoriser quelqu’un dans un procès.
fr.R: Voici d’autres paroles de gens sages : \q Un juge ne doit pas prendre parti injustement.

sw.L: Haya pia [ni maneno] ya wenye hekima. \q Kupendelea watu katika hukumu si vizuri.
sw.B: Haya pia ni maneno ya wenye hekima: \q Si haki kupendelea mtu katika kesi mahakamani.
sw.R: Haya ni maneno mengine ya watu wenye hekima: \q Mwamuzi asiegemee upande mmoja kwa udhalimu.

decisions.choice: these also are of the wise: a short added collection
decisions.reason: The heading begins a small collection (24:23–34) after the words of the wise of 22:17–24:22.

decisions.choice: to regard faces: to show partiality
decisions.reason: To "recognize the face" in court is to favor a person for who they are (18:5; 28:21; Deuteronomy 1:17; 16:19).

source.text: אֹ֤מֵ֨ר׀לְרָשָׁע֮ צַדִּ֪יק אָ֥תָּה יִקְּבֻ֥הוּ עַמִּ֑ים יִזְעָמ֥וּהוּ לְאֻמִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: [One who] says to a wicked [person], Righteous [are] you, peoples will curse him, nations will denounce him.

en.L: Whoever says to [the] wicked, "You [are] righteous," peoples will curse {{gender:them|him}}; \q nations will denounce {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: Whoever tells the guilty, "You are innocent," will be cursed by peoples \q and condemned by nations.
en.R: A judge who tells a guilty person, "You are not guilty," \q will be hated by people everywhere.

fr.L: Celui qui dit au méchant : « Tu [es] juste », les peuples le maudiront, \q les nations le condamneront.
fr.B: Celui qui dit au coupable : « Tu es innocent » sera maudit par les peuples \q et condamné par les nations.
fr.R: Un juge qui dit à un coupable : « Tu n’es pas coupable » \q sera détesté par les gens de partout.

sw.L: Yeye amwambiaye mwovu, "Wewe [ni] mwenye haki," mataifa yatamlaani; \q watu wa mataifa watamshutumu.
sw.B: Yeyote anayemwambia mwenye hatia, "Huna hatia," atalaaniwa na mataifa \q na kuhukumiwa na watu wa kila taifa.
sw.R: Mwamuzi anayemwambia mtu mwenye hatia, "Huna hatia," \q atachukiwa na watu kila mahali.

decisions.choice: wicked ... righteous: guilty and innocent in court
decisions.reason: In a court setting the words mean guilty and in the right (17:15; Isaiah 5:23).

source.text: וְלַמּוֹכִיחִ֥ים יִנְעָ֑ם וַֽ֝עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם תָּב֥וֹא בִרְכַּת־טֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: But to those who rebuke [him] it will be pleasant, and on them will come a blessing of good.

en.L: But for those who convict [the guilty] it will go well, \q and a good blessing will come on them.
en.B: But those who convict the guilty will be well thought of, \q and a rich blessing will come on them.
en.R: But things will go well for judges who punish the guilty. \q Good things will happen to them.

fr.L: Mais pour ceux qui [le] reprennent, ce sera agréable, \q et sur eux viendra une bénédiction de bonheur.
fr.B: Mais ceux qui condamnent le coupable seront estimés, \q et une riche bénédiction viendra sur eux.
fr.R: Mais tout ira bien pour les juges qui punissent les coupables. \q Il leur arrivera de bonnes choses.

sw.L: Lakini kwa wale wanaomkemea [mwenye hatia] mambo yatakwenda vizuri, \q na baraka njema itawajia.
sw.B: Lakini wale wanaomtia hatiani mwenye hatia wataheshimiwa, \q na baraka tele itawajia.
sw.R: Lakini mambo yatawaendea vizuri waamuzi wanaowaadhibu wenye hatia. \q Mambo mema yatawatokea.

decisions.choice: those who convict: who rebuke or condemn the guilty
decisions.reason: The verb (hokhiah) means to reprove or to decide against someone in a case (9:7–8; 28:23).

source.text: שְׂפָתַ֥יִם יִשָּׁ֑ק מֵ֝שִׁ֗יב דְּבָרִ֥ים נְכֹחִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Lips he kisses [one who] brings back words straightforward.

en.L: {{gender:They kiss|He kisses}} [the] lips, \q whoever gives an honest answer.
en.B: To give a straight answer \q is to kiss the lips.
en.R: An honest answer is a sign of true friendship, like a kiss.

fr.L: Il donne un baiser sur les lèvres, \q celui qui répond des paroles droites.
fr.B: Donner une réponse franche, \q c’est donner un baiser sur les lèvres.
fr.R: Une réponse honnête est un signe de vraie amitié, comme un baiser.

sw.L: Hubusu midomo, \q yeye atoaye jibu la kweli.
sw.B: Kutoa jibu lililo wazi \q ni kama kubusu midomo.
sw.R: Jibu la kweli ni ishara ya urafiki wa kweli, kama busu.

decisions.choice: kisses the lips: a sign of true friendship
decisions.reason: A kiss was a greeting of affection and loyalty (Genesis 33:4). An honest answer, even when unwelcome, is a mark of real friendship (27:6).

source.text: הָ֘כֵ֤ן בַּח֨וּץ׀מְלַאכְתֶּ֗ךָ וְעַתְּדָ֣הּ בַּשָּׂדֶ֣ה לָ֑ךְ אַ֝חַ֗ר וּבָנִ֥יתָ בֵיתֶֽךָ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Establish on the outside your work, and make it ready in the field for yourself; after, and you will build your house.

en.L: Prepare your work outside, \q and make it ready for yourself in the field; \q afterward build your house.
en.B: Get your work outside in order and your fields ready first; \q after that, build your house.
en.R: First take care of your fields and your work. \q Then you can build your house.

fr.L: Prépare ton ouvrage au-dehors, \q et apprête-le pour toi dans le champ ; \q ensuite tu bâtiras ta maison.
fr.B: Mets d’abord en ordre ton travail au-dehors et prépare tes champs ; \q après cela, bâtis ta maison.
fr.R: Occupe-toi d’abord de tes champs et de ton travail. \q Ensuite, tu pourras bâtir ta maison.

sw.L: Andaa kazi yako nje, \q na uitengeneze kwa ajili yako shambani; \q baadaye ujenge nyumba yako.
sw.B: Kwanza panga vizuri kazi yako ya nje na kuyaandaa mashamba yako; \q baada ya hapo, jenga nyumba yako.
sw.R: Kwanza shughulikia mashamba yako na kazi yako. \q Ndipo uweze kujenga nyumba yako.

decisions.choice: build your house: a home, or a family
decisions.reason: Build a house may mean to set up a home or to found a family (Ruth 4:11). Either way, make sure of a living first.

source.text: אַל־תְּהִ֣י עֵד־חִנָּ֣ם בְּרֵעֶ֑ךָ וַ֝הֲפִתִּ֗יתָ בִּשְׂפָתֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not be a witness without cause against your neighbor, and will you deceive with your lips?

en.L: Do not be a witness against your neighbor without cause, \q and do not deceive with your lips.
en.B: Do not testify against your neighbor without good reason, \q or use your lips to mislead.
en.R: Do not speak against your neighbor in court without a good reason. \q Do not lie about them.

fr.L: Ne sois pas témoin sans raison contre ton prochain, \q et ne trompe pas de tes lèvres.
fr.B: Ne témoigne pas contre ton prochain sans motif sérieux, \q et ne te sers pas de tes lèvres pour tromper.
fr.R: Ne parle pas contre ton voisin au tribunal sans bonne raison. \q Ne mens pas à son sujet.

sw.L: Usiwe shahidi dhidi ya jirani yako bila sababu, \q wala usidanganye kwa midomo yako.
sw.B: Usimshuhudie jirani yako vibaya bila sababu nzuri, \q wala usitumie midomo yako kupotosha.
sw.R: Usiseme dhidi ya jirani yako mahakamani bila sababu nzuri. \q Usiseme uongo juu yake.

decisions.choice: and will you deceive: a question with a no answer
decisions.reason: The question form is a strong warning: surely you will not deceive (Exodus 20:16).

source.text: אַל־תֹּאמַ֗ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָֽשָׂה־לִ֭י כֵּ֤ן אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לּ֑וֹ אָשִׁ֖יב לָאִ֣ישׁ כְּפָעֳלֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not say, Just as he has done to me, so I will do to him; I will repay to the person according to his deed.

en.L: Do not say, "As {{gender:they have|he has}} done to me, so I will do to {{gender:them|him}}; \q I will repay the person according to {{gender:their|his}} deed."
en.B: Do not say, "I will treat them the way they treated me; \q I will pay them back for what they did."
en.R: Do not say, "I will do to them what they did to me. \q I will get even with them."

fr.L: Ne dis pas : « Comme il m’a fait, ainsi je lui ferai ; \q je rendrai à l’homme selon son action. »
fr.B: Ne dis pas : « Je le traiterai comme il m’a traité ; \q je lui rendrai ce qu’il a fait. »
fr.R: Ne dis pas : « Je vais lui faire ce qu’il m’a fait. \q Je vais me venger. »

sw.L: Usiseme, "Kama alivyonitendea, ndivyo nitakavyomtendea; \q nitamlipa mtu huyo kwa kadiri ya tendo lake."
sw.B: Usiseme, "Nitamtendea kama alivyonitendea; \q nitamlipa kwa yale aliyoyafanya."
sw.R: Usiseme, "Nitamfanyia yale aliyonifanyia. \q Nitalipiza kisasi."

decisions.choice: I will repay: revenge belongs to God
decisions.reason: The words echo verse 12, where God repays each person by their work. Repaying is God's right, not ours (20:22; 25:21–22; Romans 12:17–19).

source.text: עַל־שְׂדֵ֣ה אִישׁ־עָצֵ֣ל עָבַ֑רְתִּי וְעַל־כֶּ֝֗רֶם אָדָ֥ם חֲסַר־לֵֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: By [the] field of a person lazy I passed by, and by [the] vineyard of a person lacking of heart.

en.L: I passed by [the] field of a sluggard, \q and by [the] vineyard of a person lacking sense,
en.B: I walked past the field of someone lazy, \q past the vineyard of someone with no sense,
en.R: One day I walked by a field that belonged to a lazy person. \q It was a vineyard of someone without any sense.

fr.L: Je suis passé près du champ d’un paresseux, \q et près de la vigne d’un homme dépourvu de sens,
fr.B: Je suis passé devant le champ d’un paresseux, \q devant la vigne d’un homme sans bon sens,
fr.R: Un jour, je suis passé près d’un champ qui appartenait à un paresseux. \q C’était la vigne de quelqu’un qui n’avait aucun bon sens.

sw.L: Nilipita karibu na shamba la mvivu, \q na karibu na shamba la mizabibu la mtu asiye na akili,
sw.B: Nilipita kando ya shamba la mtu mvivu, \q kando ya shamba la mizabibu la mtu asiye na akili,
sw.R: Siku moja nilipita karibu na shamba la mtu mvivu. \q Lilikuwa shamba la mizabibu la mtu asiye na akili hata kidogo.

decisions.choice: I passed by: the teacher tells what he saw
decisions.reason: Verses 30–34 are a short story with a lesson, like the story told in 7:6–23.

decisions.choice: passé composé for the teacher's account ("je suis passé") at every level
alternatives: passé simple ("je passai") at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: Verses 30-34 are the teacher speaking of what he saw, so they keep the tenses of speech at every level, as the French style guide sets for speech that tells a story.

decisions.choice: "le paresseux" for *atsel*, for the whole book
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets.

decisions.choice: "mvivu" for the sluggard (ʿatsel) at every level
decisions.reason: "Mvivu" is the plain Swahili word for a lazy person, the figure Proverbs mocks again and again; "mzembe" is more a careless person. This is the word used for the sluggard throughout Proverbs.

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֨ה עָ֘לָ֤ה כֻלּ֨וֹ׀קִמְּשֹׂנִ֗ים כָּסּ֣וּ פָנָ֣יו חֲרֻלִּ֑ים וְגֶ֖דֶר אֲבָנָ֣יו נֶהֱרָֽסָה׃

records.literal_gloss: and there! it had grown up all of it [with] nettles; its surface was covered [with] weeds, and the wall of its stones was broken down.

en.L: and look, it had all grown up [with] thorns; \q its surface was covered [with] nettles, \q and its stone wall was broken down.
en.B: and I saw thorns had sprung up everywhere, \q weeds had covered the ground, \q and its stone wall lay in ruins.
en.R: It was full of thorns and weeds. \q The stone wall around it had fallen down.

fr.L: et voici, tout était envahi [d’]épines ; \q sa surface était couverte [d’]orties, \q et son mur de pierres était écroulé.
fr.B: et j’ai vu que les épines avaient poussé partout, \q que les mauvaises herbes avaient couvert le sol, \q et que son mur de pierres était en ruine.
fr.R: Il était plein d’épines et de mauvaises herbes. \q Le mur de pierres qui l’entourait s’était écroulé.

sw.L: na tazama, lote lilikuwa limemea miiba; \q uso wake ulifunikwa na viwavi, \q na ukuta wake wa mawe ulikuwa umebomoka.
sw.B: nikaona miiba imeota kila mahali, \q magugu yamefunika ardhi, \q na ukuta wake wa mawe umeanguka.
sw.R: Lilikuwa limejaa miiba na magugu. \q Ukuta wa mawe uliolizunguka ulikuwa umeanguka.

decisions.choice: thorns ... nettles: weeds that take over neglected land
decisions.reason: The exact plants are uncertain (Isaiah 34:13; Job 30:7). The broken wall leaves the vineyard open to animals and thieves (Isaiah 5:5).

source.text: וָֽאֶחֱזֶ֣ה אָ֭נֹכִֽי אָשִׁ֣ית לִבִּ֑י רָ֝אִ֗יתִי לָקַ֥חְתִּי מוּסָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And I saw, I; I set my heart; I saw, I received instruction.

en.L: Then I looked; I took [it] to heart; \q I saw [and] received instruction:
en.B: I looked at it and thought it over; \q I saw it and learned a lesson:
en.R: I looked and thought about it. \q Then I learned this lesson:

fr.L: Alors j’ai regardé ; j’[y] ai appliqué mon cœur ; \q j’ai vu, [et] j’ai reçu une leçon :
fr.B: J’ai regardé et j’y ai réfléchi ; \q j’ai vu et j’en ai tiré une leçon :
fr.R: J’ai regardé et j’ai réfléchi. \q Alors j’ai appris cette leçon :

sw.L: Ndipo nikatazama; nikaweka [jambo hilo] moyoni; \q niliona [nikapokea] mafundisho:
sw.B: Nililitazama na kulitafakari; \q niliona, nikajifunza somo hili:
sw.R: Nilitazama na kulifikiria. \q Kisha nikajifunza somo hili:

decisions.choice: I saw ... received instruction: learning from what is seen
decisions.reason: The teacher learns by watching the world, as in 6:6. The lesson follows in verses 33–34.

source.text: מְעַ֣ט שֵׁ֭נוֹת מְעַ֣ט תְּנוּמ֑וֹת מְעַ֓ט׀חִבֻּ֖ק יָדַ֣יִם לִשְׁכָּֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of hands to rest,

en.L: A little sleep, a little slumber, \q a little folding of [the] hands to rest,
en.B: a bit more sleep, a bit more dozing, \q a bit more lying with arms folded,
en.R: A lazy person says, "Let me sleep a little longer. \q Let me rest a little more."

fr.L: Un peu de sommeil, un peu d’assoupissement, \q un peu croiser les mains pour se reposer,
fr.B: encore un peu de sommeil, encore un peu de somnolence, \q encore un peu les bras croisés pour dormir,
fr.R: Le paresseux dit : « Laisse-moi dormir encore un peu. \q Laisse-moi me reposer encore un moment. »

sw.L: Usingizi kidogo, kusinzia kidogo, \q kukunja mikono kidogo ili kupumzika,
sw.B: kulala kidogo zaidi, kusinzia kidogo zaidi, \q kulala kidogo zaidi mikono ikiwa imekunjwa,
sw.R: Mvivu husema, "Niache nilale kidogo zaidi. \q Niache nipumzike kidogo tena."

decisions.choice: a little sleep: repeating 6:10
decisions.reason: Verses 33–34 repeat 6:10–11 almost word for word. What the teacher saw in the field confirms the older saying.

decisions.choice: A lazy person says
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that these are the lazy person's own excuses, as at 6:10.

source.text: וּבָֽא־מִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ רֵישֶׁ֑ךָ וּ֝מַחְסֹרֶ֗יךָ כְּאִ֣ישׁ מָגֵֽן׃פ

records.literal_gloss: and will come going about your poverty, and your lacks like a man of shield.

en.L: and your poverty will come [on you] walking about, \q and your needs like a man with a shield.
en.B: and poverty will be on you like a drifter on the road, \q and need like a man with a shield.
en.R: Then you will suddenly become poor, \q as if a robber had come and taken everything you have.

fr.L: et ta pauvreté viendra [sur toi] en rôdeur, \q et tes besoins comme un homme armé d’un bouclier.
fr.B: et la pauvreté tombera sur toi comme un vagabond sur la route, \q et le besoin comme un homme armé d’un bouclier.
fr.R: Alors tu deviendras pauvre tout à coup, \q comme si un voleur était venu te prendre tout ce que tu as.

sw.L: na umaskini wako utakuja [juu yako] ukitembea, \q na mahitaji yako kama mtu mwenye ngao.
sw.B: na umaskini utakujia kama mzururaji njiani, \q na uhitaji kama mtu mwenye ngao.
sw.R: Ndipo utakuwa maskini ghafula, \q kana kwamba mnyang'anyi amekuja na kuchukua kila kitu ulicho nacho.

decisions.choice: walking about ... a man with a shield: as in 6:11
decisions.reason: The wording differs slightly from 6:11 ("walking about" rather than "like one walking about", and "needs" in the plural), with the same sense: poverty arrives like a raider and cannot be fought off.
